newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - HFS, Black form real estate venture.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - HFS, Black form real estate venture.

text.p: Powerhouse real estate and travel company HFS Inc announced plans on Tuesday to expand in the real estate brokerage business through a new venture with investor Leon Black.
Already the world's largest franchisor of residential real estate brokerage offices, Parsippany, N.J.-based HFS said the fragmented industry is ripe for consolidation.

Under the deal announced Tuesday, HFS will invest $157 million of the $232 million in initial funding slated for the venture, called NRT Inc. Black's Apollo Managment L.P. and other institutions will invest $75 million.
When the deal is completed, NRT together with other assets will have about $575 million in cash and other funds for acquisitions.

"The strategy of NRT is to grow very quickly by acquiring large regional independents who have already begun the process of consolidation on a regional basis," HFS Chairman Henry Silverman said in a telephone interview.

NRT's first acquisition will be the purchase of National Realty Trust, which is the nation's largest residential real estate brokerage and HFS's largest real estate franchisee with 1996 sales of about $700 million.
National Realty Trust owns and operates 400 residential realty offices under HFS' Century 21, Coldwell Banker and ERA franchise systems.
Terms of the acquisition were not disclosed. NRT expects to complete the purchase of National Realty Trust by the end of August.

The companies said the new venture already has reached agreements with several other large real estate brokerages for additional acquisitions. They did not identify the properties or the terms and said the deals are subject to reaching definitive agreements and other conditions.
"We expect that NRT will complete substantial acquisition activity by the end of 1997 and anticipate an expansion of its activites thereafter," Silverman said.
He said the venture will likely focus its efforts around the U.S., adding "you want to fish where the fish are biting."
Apollo considers the new venture a long-term investment opportunity in a consolidating industry, a spokesman said.
The companies said NRT will use its capital mainly to acquire residential real estate brokerage offices not affiliated with HFS and convert them to HFS franchises.
In addition, they said NRT will use PHH Mortgage Services, a unit of HFS, to be the sole mortgage lender in NRT offices.
Industry sources said HFS previously suggested to the investment community that it was considering the move.

"You build credibility with your franchisees by being in the same business with them. They'll understand business better and they'll help grow the business by understanding it better and being a participant in it," said Mitch Roschelle, a partner in the real estate advisory business of Coopers & Lybrand.

The move is the latest expansion bid by HFS, whose lodging franchises include Ramada, Howard Johnson's, Days Inn and Super 8 Motels. The company has filed an intial public offering for its Avis rental car subsidiary, which earlier this week agreed to buy a major franchisee in California and the Southwest for about $195 million.
In one of the biggest deals announced this year, HFS in May agreed to an $11 billion stock-swap merger with direct marketing giant CUC International Inc.
